Yield strength (YS) in Ni-based ODS alloys can be estimated according to the sum of friction strength σ0 (8 MPa) [29], solution strengthening ΔσS, grain boundary strengthening ΔσG, dislocation strengthening ΔσD, γ′ phase strengthening Δσγ’ and oxide dispersion strengthening ΔσOro.
The fine grain strengthening ΔσG can be obtained using subsequent formula [38]: ΔσG = kD−1/2
The dislocation strengthening ΔσD, which is a function of dislocation density ρ, can be expressed according to Bailey-Hirsch formula [32]: ΔσD = αMGbρ1/2

γ′ phases are softer compared with oxide particles in ODS superalloys. Thence, it is generally speaking that the dislocations distributed in alloys interact with fine γ′ phase through shearing way [42].
The Orowan strengthening ΔσOro, which is originated from pinning of hard oxide particle to dislocations and grain boundaries, is a vital important strengthening method for Ni-based ODS alloys.
It is generally considered that high grain boundary density deteriorated mechanical properties at elevated temperature due to occurrence of grain boundary sliding [45].
For all alloys, the contribution of Orowan strengthening σo derived from oxides is the highest among all strengthening mechanisms, accounting for approximately 40% of total yield stress at RT.
